REQ-020 (registration for an open event with atomic capacity enforcement and qr_token issuance, GitHub issue #23, second requirement of Phase 4) had RELEASE-VALIDATOR PASS at Step 5 (commit 2066d8f, 'chore(WF02-REQ-020): Step 5 release validation -- PASS'). Verified the factual claims directly against the real code before writing the status-history note, rather than trusting the task prompt's summary: read apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts directly and confirmed decideRegistrationOutcome() is the pure first-match-wins outcome table, generateQrToken() is exactly randomBytes(32).toString('hex') with zero parameters (never derived from the user id, never Math.random), and registerForEvent() opens its db.transaction with a real `tx.select(...).from(events)...for("update")` row lock held for the transaction's lifetime before reading/counting/deciding/writing -- a genuine SELECT ... FOR UPDATE atomic sequence, not read-then-write. Confirmed writeAuditLog() runs exactly once per admitted/waitlisted outcome inside the same tx, and every non-writing outcome returns before that section. Confirmed apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts implements the register:<eventId> callback per the requirement's scope. Confirmed no schema change was needed (registrations.qr_token/source already existed from REQ-011, per `git log` on this branch showing no new drizzle migration file). Confirmed docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-020 entry (description + 6 acceptance criteria) already matched the shipped mechanism exactly -- no content correction needed.

Checked README.md (grep for registration/qr_token/capacity/apps-bot terms) -- still contains no bot-flow-specific content beyond the one generic apps/bot description line from REQ-009's doc-update step, so no README update was made -- same checked-then-skipped pattern as every prior bot requirement (REQ-010 through REQ-019).
